headline: Zurich's Chiara Bättig wants to enter Formula 1: Will she be the woman who beats everyone?
lead: Within a very short time, the 16-year-old traded her go-kart for a 180-horsepower racing car. Her goal: the top class.
seo_title: Formula 1: Perhaps a woman from Zurich will soon be driving in the premier class
social_title: Women in Formula 1: A woman from Zurich wants to make the leap into the premier class
print_title: A Zurich native on her way to the top league
print_subtitle: Chiara Bättig, 16, wants to establish herself permanently as a woman in Formula 1
summary_bullets_en: 16-year-old Zurich native Chiara Bättig is a rising talent in the Red Bull Junior Team, competing in British Formula 3.
She impressed at the Red Bull casting in Estoril despite having no prior experience with Formula 4 cars.
Her goal is to become the first woman to establish herself in Formula 1 and compete at the highest level.
key_questions_de: Wie will Chiara Bättig den Sprung in die Formel 1 schaffen?
Welche Herausforderungen prägen den Weg von Frauen im Motorsport?
Wie beeinflusst Red Bull Bättigs Karriereentwicklung?

teaser_image.caption: Within a very short time, the 16-year-old traded her go-kart for a 180-horsepower racing car. Her goal: the top class.

original_de.headline: Die Zürcherin Chiara Bättig will in die Formel 1: Wird sie die Frau, die alle schlägt?
original_de.lead: Innerhalb kürzester Zeit tauschte die 16-Jährige den Gokart gegen einen 180-PS-Rennwagen. Das Ziel: die Königsklasse.

body.caption: From the gravel trap directly to the Red Bull junior team: Chiara Bättig impressed a year ago in Estoril, Portugal.

body.text: The trip to the kart track was meant to be only a little variety during the holidays. Chiara Bättig, then five years old, enjoyed herself for the first time with the nearly 6 hp vehicles. Initially, she was all alone on the track, then two boys, eight and ten, joined her. Her mother, Natascha Kessler, feared that the afternoon would end in tears. And it did. But it was the boys who cried, because of the fast girl.

The early holiday love for motorsport continues to thrive. Today, at age 16, the Zurich native is one of the talents that the Formula 1 racing team Red Bull trains in its junior team for more advanced roles. She races in British Formula 3, one of the toughest junior championships. Her dream aligns with that of Formula 1 organizers: in the near future, a woman is finally set to make a permanent leap into the premier class.
Not just fast, but faster than others

Social networks and especially the Netflix series «Drive to Survive» ensure that almost 40% of the audience at Grand Prix racetracks are female. Motorsport is one of the few disciplines where women and men can compete against each other in the same class. In theory, at least, it depends only on talent and the right conditions. In this technical sport, that inevitably means finances must be in order. Even in the entry-level series, sums between 100,000 and 400,000 Swiss francs are required. This significantly exceeds the budgets of average households; a privately funded Formula 4 season easily exceeds the million-franc mark.

For Chiara Bättig, too, an early decision had to be made: she equally enjoyed skiing, playing tennis, wakeboarding and karting – but she had to concentrate on one of them. Her parents were sure that their daughter would choose something other than motorsport. They were wrong. «I don’t just want to be fast, I want to be faster than everyone else. And above all, I love the direct confrontation with others on the racetrack,» Bättig says. At the time, the Bättigs did not yet realize that karting is the basic training for every Formula 1 career.

body.caption: The Zurich native impresses as a rookie in the demanding Formula 4.

body.text: At age eight, Bättig drove her first official kart races, and at age twelve, she became the youngest in history to win the Swiss Junior Championship. She is the only one to have won the title in the category three times in a row. She truly attracted attention at age 15 at the European Kart Championship. Less for individual results than for consistent lap times. Scouts from several Formula 1 teams, who already search for talent in school categories with a closely integrated network, had her on their radar.

This eventually led to an invitation from Red Bull last year for a scouting session in Estoril, Portugal. Among the twelve candidates, Bättig was the only one who had never driven a 180 hp Formula 4 racing car. However, this only became evident after she had stalled the car eight times. When she finally got going, she landed in the gravel trap on the very first corner.

body.caption: Chiara Bättig possesses a typical racing driver attribute: she is self-driven.

body.text: It was a crash test for her psyche, but also an opportunity to show how she handles increased pressure. At the end of the scouting session, Bättig was ahead of many of the more experienced boys, thanks to her ability to adapt to the car and track better with each lap, continuously improving her times. Some of the aspirants were sent home after the first day. A real shoot-out. Bättig was the only one accepted into the beverage company's junior team, which is distributed across various Formula classes. From the legendary Red Bull talent scout Helmut Marko, she first received one of his rare compliments – and then a training contract. The Austrian was a major patron of Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen, who made it from karting to world championship titles through the junior development program.
Will she be the woman who beats everyone?

On the website of British Formula 4, there are two remarkable statements from Bättig: Asked about her favorite female athlete, she names herself – in ten years. Where does she want to be in five years? «In Formula 1.» Indeed, the racing driver is now at a point where healthy self-confidence is absolutely necessary, but also the effective management of her own ambition.

Formula 4 is already a complex racing series that requires technology, intuition, tactics, mental strength and calculated risk awareness. It is a kind of mini-Formula 1. The season unfolds over ten race weekends, each with three races in Great Britain, plus a winter series. This makes Bättig a perpetual commuter. Travel strains, motorsport and schoolwork: she is self-driven, a typical racing driver attribute.

The fact that she is one of the few women who have so far received a real chance for advancement does not bother her. Rather, it is still something special for others. She knows that she must earn respect in a sport long dominated by a macho culture: «Most have learned to accept me over the season.» After two-thirds of the season, she ranks 15th as a rookie in the British championship – out of 38 starters. It is a large and competitive field; many Grand Prix racing teams test young talent here. The competition remains fierce, and it will not get any easier. Her parents say: «Chiara possesses an unwavering belief in herself.»

While her results so far are decent for a rookie, they are not enough for her: «I always want to be at the limit.» The thrill that it could all end with one wrong steering movement is part of it. Occasionally, she has to balance her strong will with reason: «At the beginning, I always went from zero to a hundred; now I am more focused on easing into it.» «But as quickly as possible,» she adds. After each race, she must send a report to the headquarters in Milton Keynes. The headquarters determines whether and where she will continue her career next year.

Racing drivers usually complete three seasons in the lower Formula classes; few manage to progress directly. Her next goal would be Formula 3, which tours the world with the premier class. The fact that she can only advance with further exceptional performances does not deter Bättig. She deals pragmatically with the necessary assertiveness: «Either you are fast or you are not fast.» Red Bull has brought over twenty talents into Formula 1, maintaining its own junior team there, the Racing Bulls, but there is naturally no guarantee. For example, Vaud native Sébastien Buemi made it to a cockpit, while Neel Jani, from Eastern Switzerland, did not. Both Swiss drivers found great success at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

For Bättig's idol Max Verstappen, whose mother was an excellent kart racer, it is not about gender, but about determination. «There are simply fewer women who start this sport. Therefore, the percentage who make it to the top is naturally lower.» However, the Dutchman is certain: «No team principal would take a man if there was a woman who beats everyone at the same time.»

An important currency in motorsport is attention, right from the start. Formula 1 has launched the Formula Academy for this purpose: a women-only series that competes as part of many Grand Prix events. In Silverstone, Bättig was allowed to compete with her female colleagues on a wild card entry in front of 175,000 spectators. She immediately secured pole position as the youngest driver in the Academy's history and finished second in the race. Academy head Susie Wolff, the last woman to compete in a Formula 1 weekend in 2015, offered her one piece of advice: «Just have fun here.» Thanks to her ability to adapt rapidly, Bättig also became faster with each lap here. It can hardly be attributed solely to her sharing a birthday with Ayrton Senna.

body.caption: The focus is forward: Chiara Bättig wants to race in Formula 1 in five years at the latest.

body.text: She did not really experience much of Formula 1 in the hustle and bustle of Silverstone. It was a good thing she had organized her very first Grand Prix visit on her own initiative shortly before. Her parents had insisted she take two weeks of vacation in Tuscany in June, a deliberate break from racing.

However, that only worked until their daughter found out that it was only a few hours by train from Pisa to Monte Carlo. Experiencing the live premiere at the classic event itself was entirely different from the race afternoons she spent as a child next to her grandfather on the sofa. Hardly back at her holiday resort from Monaco, she was already off on tour with friends – this time to the 24 Hours of Le Mans. No, slowing down is simply not Chiara Bättig's thing.
